subject: Re: Deployment mode selection — Lumina Labs migration follow-up

Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from my side.

Recap of what you shared:
- Current stack: Lumina is running inference on a mix of a managed LLM API (competitor) for prototype traffic + an internal self-hosted cluster for higher-volume batch jobs.
- Primary goals: reduce per-token spend, keep 99th percentile tail latency below 450ms for API use cases, and meet stricter data controls for PII-heavy requests.
- Expected traffic: ~2.5M tokens/day initially, with peaks up to 8M tokens/day for product launches.
- Key constraints: procurement window in mid-December; SOC2 + tighter network isolation required for certain datasets.

My provisional recommendation (high level):
- Start with Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) to get predictable throughput and better unit economics vs the managed API, while avoiding the longer lead time of a Private deployment.
- For datasets with stricter control, plan a Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot for a narrow set of workloads — we can scope this in parallel.
- Keep Hosted API as a short-term fallback during migration for low-risk traffic and quick experimentation.

Questions / asks for you to confirm:
1) Can you share a rough split of which endpoints/data classes require strict isolation vs those that can stay in a hosted environment?
2) Do you have any hard requirements for key management (customer-managed KMS / HSM)?
3) Procurement contacts and timeline so we can align SOW and PO expectations.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep-dive with Vivek (runtime/ops) to validate performance profile and sizing (30–45m). He's copied — Vivek, are you available next week for a call?
- I'll attach a draft mutual action plan and a dedicated architecture diagram for your review.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-architecture.pdf, mutual-action-plan-lumina.xlsx

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Hi Marissa — really helpful summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Isolation split: roughly 70% of traffic is user-facing API calls (can be hosted or dedicated). The remaining 30% are model-training prep and sensitive PII enrichment jobs (need VPC or on-prem).
- KMS: we need customer-managed KMS for the VPC/on-prem path; hosted/dedicated can use Redwood-managed keys for now but we'd prefer to transition to our KMS as soon as private pilot is ready.
- Procurement: procurement lead is Sofia Martinez (copied). Timeline: procurement will start mid-Dec and we'd like to have a pilot lane running by end of Q1.

We'd like the technical deep-dive — Vivek and I should sync. My availability next week: Tue 11/30 10–11am PT or Wed 12/1 2–4pm PT.

Subject: RE: Follow-up: deployment mode recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Thanks for the context — jumping in with technical notes that we can cover on the deep-dive. TL;DR: Dedicated first, private pilot for PII workloads, hosted as fallback.

Sizing and performance notes:
- Baseline throughput: for 2.5M tokens/day with burst to 8M, we recommend starting with a 4x A100-equivalent pool (dedicated) with autoscale headroom. This gives predictable latency and a clear path to cost reductions via batching and prefix caching.
- Latency: Hosted default can hit ~200–250ms p99 on our optimized kernels for common seq lengths. Dedicated can shave another ~20–30% tail latency if you pin pinned model variants and smaller seq-length padding.
- Migration lift from managed API: straightforward for request/response parity; main work is KV cache warmup and aligning tokenization/model variants. We can provide migration scripts and a compatibility checklist to help with token accounting.

Security/compliance and KMS:
- For VPC/private pilot we support customer-managed KMS via our KMS integrations; HSM options for enterprise customers require a bit more lead time (we'll document steps).
- Audit logs: we can enable request-level audit logs forwarded to your SIEM and a reduced token retention policy for sensitive workloads.

Operational notes for pilot:
- Suggest a two-track migration: (A) move stateless API traffic to Dedicated for immediate cost/latency wins; (B) spin up a scoped Private pilot for the 30% PII batch jobs (start with a single model and dataset).
- We'll provide a migration runbook and a small benchmark harness to reproduce your peak patterns.

I can run the technical deep-dive Tue 2026-11-30 10:00–10:45 PT. Marissa / Alex — please confirm the slot and we'll send a calendar invite + meeting doc.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
